# 1. Introduction
The purpose of this paper is to present a new method for solving the problem of finding the maximum number of non-attacking queens on an $n \times n$ chessboard. This problem has been studied extensively, and various algorithms have been proposed over the years. However, most existing methods are either computationally expensive or do not scale well with increasing board sizes.
In this work, we propose a novel approach that combines elements of dynamic programming and constraint satisfaction techniques. Our method leverages the structure of the problem to efficiently explore the solution space while ensuring that all constraints are satisfied. We demonstrate that our algorithm can find optimal solutions for boards up to size $n = 14$ in a fraction of the time required by traditional backtracking methods.
The rest of this paper is organized as follows: Section 2 provides a brief overview of related work and discusses the challenges associated with solving the N-Queens problem. Section 3 describes our proposed algorithm in detail, including its key components and implementation details. Section 4 presents experimental results comparing our method against existing approaches. Finally, Section 5 concludes the paper and outlines future directions for research.
# 2. Related Work
The N-Queens problem is a classic example of a constraint satisfaction problem (CSP). It involves placing $n$ queens on an $n \times n$ chessboard such that no two queens threaten each other. A queen can attack any piece in the same row, column, or diagonal. Therefore, the goal is to place the queens so that no two queens share the same row, column, or diagonal.
Several algorithms have been developed to solve this problem:
1. **Backtracking**: This is one of the earliest and most straightforward approaches. It works by recursively trying to place queens row by row, backtracking whenever a conflict is detected. While simple to implement, it can be very slow for larger board sizes due to the exponential growth of the search space.
